video_title: Will Bitcoin Survive Quantum Computing? | Jordi Visser
gist: Jordi Visser argues quantum won't kill Bitcoin (a 20-40 year hardware problem) while a historic hedge-fund unwind hits AI stocks, which he calls inevitable not a bubble, and names Eli Lilly his top long as a non-cyclical AI-proof hedge.

insights.claim: Jordi Visser rejects Chamath's claim that quantum computing takes Bitcoin to zero, citing Adam Back's view that quantum is a hardware bottleneck with a 20-40 year horizon (others say 5-7), leaving time for the Bitcoin community to respond.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Treat quantum as a slow-moving, addressable risk rather than a near-term reason to exit Bitcoin.

insights.claim: The quantum bottleneck is the physical world, the same constraint currently slowing AI development and usage, so quantum progress will be paced by hardware.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Hardware milestones, not headlines, are the signal to track for quantum timelines.

insights.claim: Crisis accelerates crisis management: ongoing AI-agent-driven hacking and banks moving onto crypto guardrails give JPMorgan and other banks a vested interest in speeding up a post-quantum cryptographic solution for Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Institutional adoption of Bitcoin raises the incentive to fund quantum-resistant upgrades.

insights.claim: Bitcoin held roughly $80-85K through a week of oil near $115, AI-trade sell-offs and quantum headlines, which Pompliano reads as a strong relative-strength signal heading into year-end.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Bitcoin's resilience to multiple shocks is a bullish tell worth watching alongside equities.

insights.claim: Pompliano argues the good guys with more money generally beat the bad guys in the technology cat-and-mouse game, even as AI gives attackers abundant intelligence and time, so cybersecurity becomes a major issue but not an existential one for Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Cybersecurity spend and AI-defense tools are a structural beneficiary.

themes.theme: AI agents and the cyber threat

insights.claim: Agent swarms can crack reused passwords in seconds, so hacking has surged only in the past year since agent swarms became available; Visser cites Axios reports of banks being hacked at record pace and unvetted AI agents accessing US bank accounts.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect rising security incidents and demand for identity/authentication upgrades at financial institutions.

themes.theme: Hedge fund unwind and AI-stock sell-off

insights.claim: October is a historic month of losses for hedge funds, worse than July, because damage is broad across credit, rates, regions and equity strategies, eliminating diversification benefits for levered multi-strategy funds.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Forced deleveraging explains indiscriminate selling, including in AI leaders, rather than a change in fundamentals.

insights.claim: Goldman reported only three days since 2020 when long/short equity, quant and multi-strat were all down over 80bp; all three came this year, and a fourth on Thursday hit over 1% for each.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Synchronized losses across strategies signal a crowded-positioning unwind.

insights.claim: The French-German bond spread carry trade (about 125bp, levered) has been unwinding for seven weeks, with the first four days of this week larger than the 2011-12 EU crisis week; combined with CoreWeave debt stress this hit multi-strat books.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch OAT-Bund spreads and AI-infrastructure credit as indicators of unwind progress.

insights.claim: Visser compares the current deleveraging to LTCM and the August 2007 quant quake, and says the best-performing 20 stocks of the year fell 5-10% in a day while still up 100%+.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Historical analogs suggest sharp, liquidity-driven air pockets that can reverse quickly.

insights.claim: Visser expects the low for the AI-stock sell-off within about two weeks, with catalysts being hyperscaler earnings, the midterm elections and the Treasury quarterly refunding announcement; the S&P 500 is still up over 12% year-to-date.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Mark the three catalyst dates for a potential tactical re-entry into AI names.

insights.claim: Pompliano expects uncertainty around the midterms to lift once they occur, with markets likely strong into year-end.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Election-driven overhang could clear in November.

insights.claim: Visser asserts AI is not a bubble but inevitable; corrections or multi-year delays (like the 4-year gap between the dot-com bottom and the iPhone) can happen, but there are no free lunches in markets.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Buy-the-dip framing for AI, with accepted drawdown risk.
insights.quote: AI is not a bubble. It's inevitable. End of story.

insights.claim: Citing Marc Andreessen, attitudes to new technology follow age: under ~25 it is just part of life, 25-35 it is a tool for making money, and above ~35 it is viewed as evil, which explains perma-bears on AI and crypto.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Older allocators may systematically underweight new technology; the young are native users.

insights.claim: Andreessen said the gap between AI-native companies and incumbents has never been wider and keeps widening.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Favor AI-native challengers over incumbents when assessing disruption exposure.

insights.claim: a16z renamed its crypto fund category to 'frontier', reflecting that crypto and AI technologies are merging and the equity-versus-token distinction is blurring.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Venture capital is bundling crypto and AI; investors should expect converging asset classes.

insights.claim: Dan Ives told Visser the answer to AI bears is to go to Korea and see the demand; Pompliano argues bubble debates need the demand side, not just capex spending like Meta's.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Track end-demand indicators (Korean memory/semis) instead of only spending headlines.

insights.claim: Pompliano says AI is already smarter than he is and that the new investment 'one big idea' is that AI is smarter than us, so winning comes from how deeply one integrates AI into work and life, not just from owning hyperscalers.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Individual AI penetration is an edge; the same logic implies pressure on traditional discretionary managers.

insights.claim: Pompliano used an AI agent to plan the sale of a stalled commercial property; it built comps and also produced a target list of local land buyers, a step the owner had never considered.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Agents surface non-obvious outbound-sales strategies that humans skip.

insights.claim: Active AI usage (typing a prompt) is less valuable than passive usage (meetings recorded, notes auto-generated and stored as context), and passive-plus-automation points to autonomous processes inside companies.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Products that embed passively and keep memory may capture the most enterprise value.

insights.claim: Pompliano's public company has more AI agents than employees and is extending them from analytics and engineering into finance and operations, with the agents also brainstorming further use cases.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Agent-to-employee ratios are an emerging productivity metric for evaluating companies.

insights.claim: Memory is the key AI asset: back up an assistant's memory to Google Drive, Notion or Obsidian so multiple AI models can share context and users can switch models freely.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Model switching costs fall when memory is portable, pressuring lock-in moats.

insights.claim: Visser recommends using AI as a weekly life coach and daily gratitude journal that asks recurring questions and reviews progress over 30 days, framing AI usage as compounding.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Behavioral stickiness of personal-memory AI products supports long-term engagement.

insights.claim: A prominent New York law school bans all laptops and phones from classrooms; Visser sees this as institutions failing to adapt, and says his college-junior son's internship value comes from building agentic workflow solutions during meetings, making a degree less critical.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Education and legal-training incumbents face disruption; AI-native skills command a premium.

insights.claim: Eli Lilly made new all-time highs in a week when AI stocks fell, and Visser predicts it becomes the largest US company within five years; he calls it his biggest long, ahead of Nvidia and Marvell.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Eli Lilly is positioned as a defensive-growth hedge to the AI trade.

insights.claim: Eli Lilly has risen 10 straight years with over 30% CAGR, while nearly all big tech fell in 2022; healthcare is 22-23% of personal consumption versus under 3% for energy, is non-cyclical, and is funded by government and insurers.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Healthcare's scale and non-cyclicality support a rotation if the AI build-out stalls.

insights.claim: Nvidia's multiple is compressing because the market prices eventual disruption in five years, and it and Micron remain cyclical, exposed to over-purchased GPUs and power constraints.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Power availability is the binding constraint on GPU demand durability.

insights.claim: Pharma is migrating from low-multiple safe stocks to growth stocks as AI-driven drug discovery and breakthroughs get mispriced; Eli Lilly's TuneLab platform has 135 companies feeding IP into a shared supercomputer.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: AI-enabled pharma and biotech collaboration platforms could re-rate the sector.

insights.claim: Former OpenAI Chief Product Officer Kevin Weil launched Warp Sciences to operate at the intersection of AI, biotech and healthcare.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Signals talent flow from AI labs into AI-bio.

insights.claim: Palmer Luckey's Anduril and a biotech firm are collaborating on 'War Hounds', genetically modified battlefield dogs equipped with Anduril gear, reportedly valued at a billion dollars at launch.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Defense-tech valuations reflect ambitious, frontier-bio bets.
